text:
marie (cs): FYI got an escalation from a customer — their rerank responses sometimes contain negative scores and values >1. They expected 0-1 probabilities.

sam (support): Copy of the customer's example payload and response they sent: 
```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "query": "best coffee maker",
  "candidates": ["A", "B", "C"]
}

200 OK
{
  "results": [
    {"id": 0, "score": -1.84},
    {"id": 1, "score": 0.12},
    {"id": 2, "score": 2.4}
  ]
}
```

sam (support): They say their client treats score as probability and the downstream ranking looks wrong. They want guidance asap, billing is impacted.

eli (ml): This is expected behavior for our current reranker: we return raw relevance logits (un-normalized). Negative values are fine; scores are on an arbitrary scale dependent on model head and temperature. We should verify docs though — I thought we had a note.

marie (cs): Customer says doc wasn't clear. They only saw a line about "scores" but no semantics or recommended client-side transform.

eli (ml): Quick repro steps for us: use same model + input, check output distribution. Example python client to compute softmax: 
```python
import math
scores = [-1.84, 0.12, 2.4]
exp = [math.exp(s) for s in scores]
probs = [e / sum(exp) for e in exp]
print(probs)  # softmax normalized probabilities
```
This will convert to 0-1 and sum-to-1. If they want independent confidence per candidate (not a distribution), use sigmoid on each score instead.

marie (cs): Good phrasing for the customer: "Our rerank API returns raw model scores (logits). These are not normalized probabilities. To convert to probabilities, apply softmax across candidates; to get independent per-item confidences, apply sigmoid to each score." Can someone confirm?

eli (ml): Confirm. Also mention negative/large magnitudes depend on model calibration and temperature. We should also list edge cases: when candidates vary by length you may want length-normalization or to use pairwise scoring.

aaron (infra): Quick thought — is there any case where we should return normalized scores server-side? Some customers asked for a flag in the API to request normalized output. We don't have that yet. It's a small product request.

marie (cs): Customer asked for a short-term workaround: they're going to softmax client-side. Long-term they want an opt-in API param.

sam (support): Action items I propose: 
- Triage as P2 internal doc bug and product request.
- Provide the customer a snippet + recommended transform.
- Open a small enhancement ticket for an optional "score_normalization" query param (none|softmax|sigmoid|minmax).

marie (cs): I already pasted eli's python snippet and added a JS snippet: 
```js
const scores = [-1.84, 0.12, 2.4];
const exps = scores.map(s => Math.exp(s));
const sum = exps.reduce((a,b)=>a+b, 0);
const probs = exps.map(e => e/sum);
console.log(probs); // normalized probabilities
```
Customer responded: "thanks this helps, please add a param so we don't have to maintain transforms".

eli (ml): For docs wording: short bullets + one-line code for softmax and sigmoid + note about when to use each. Also show example of non-normalized output so customers don't get surprised.

aaron (infra): I'll create a tracking ticket in product board for the API flag and flag for backwards compatibility. If we add normalization server-side it must be opt-in and explicit.

marie (cs): Sam — can you mark this thread as resolved for now after sending the snippets, and open the product ticket? I'll follow up with the customer regarding timeline.

sam (support): Done, sent snippets and guidance. I'll create ticket and paste link here when done.

rerank-bot: Ticket created: RERANK-4921 - add optional score_normalization param (none|softmax|sigmoid|minmax) — https://redwood.atlassian.example/browse/RERANK-4921 :white_check_mark:

marie (cs): Awesome, thanks everyone. We should also schedule a tiny docs patch (docs.rerank -> semantics) so future customers don't hit this.

eli (ml): I'll draft a 2-paragraph explanation and sample code to drop into the API reference.

sam (support): Last note for internal triage: add a unit test to ensure examples in docs match current model outputs (pre/post norm) so we don't drift.

marie (cs): Closing thread — will reopen if customer needs more. :thumbsup:
